summary: Bismuth titanate thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with bismuth tris(bis(trimethylsilyl)amide) and titanium methoxide as precursors, and water as the oxygen source. The films were postannealed to crystallize into the ferroelectric Bi4Ti3O12 phase, showing remanent polarization and coercive field values. The study focused on the ALD process, film morphology, and electrical properties of the resulting Bi4Ti3O12 films.
evidence: Bismuth titanate thin films were prepared by atomic layer deposition. Bismuth tris(bis(trimethylsilyl)-amide) Bi(N(SiMe3)2)3 was used as the bismuth and titanium methoxide Ti(OMe)4 as the titanium precursor while water was used as the oxygen source. Self-limited growth of Bi-Ti-O films took place at a deposition temperature of 190°C. The Bi-Ti-O films postannealed at 750 °C crystallized to either pyrochlore Bi2Ti2O7-type structures, mixtures of the pyrochlore- and layered perovskite Bi4Ti3O12 phases, or phase-pure Bi4Ti3O12 depending on the Bi/(Bi + Ti) ratio in the film. After postannealing in O2 at 600 °C 51 nm thick films deposited on Pt/SiO2/Si substrates had a remanent polarization Pr and coercive field Ec of 0.5 íC/cm2 and 24 kV/cm, respectively.
